payload.reason: The authors suggest that Twitter data provides a better representation of language use due to its broad coverage and the nature of language usage in tweets, which can reflect real-time language dynamics that census data may miss.

claims.text: Twitter data offers a better representation of language use because it captures real-time dynamics and includes languages not reflected in census data, leading to a higher true positive rate for common languages like English and Spanish.

The methodology of collecting tweets from a wide area without biasing by language-specific keywords allows for a more accurate representation of language use in different countries compared to web-crawled data.
